instructions: Independent work. No hints or answer key during testing. Ask for clarification; substantive teaching makes the item assisted and requires a fresh replacement. Three questions per batch. Calculator allowed for arithmetic after writing the exact setup; no solver or answer lookup.

items.objective: Choose and calculate measures of center; explain outlier sensitivity.
items.prompt: For 1, 4, 4, 6, 10, find mean, median, and mode.

items.objective: Choose and calculate measures of center; explain outlier sensitivity.
items.prompt: Replace 10 by 40. What are the new mean and median, and why do they behave differently?

items.objective: Calculate population variance and distinguish it from sample variance.
items.prompt: Treat 1, 4, 7 as a population. Calculate its variance.

items.objective: Calculate population variance and distinguish it from sample variance.
items.prompt: Treat those same observations as a sample. Calculate the usual sample variance.

items.objective: Recover the data’s units and interpret spread without assuming normality.
items.prompt: A population has variance 49 seconds². Find its standard deviation.

items.objective: Recover the data’s units and interpret spread without assuming normality.
items.prompt: A data set has standard deviation 5. Transform every value by y=-2x+1. Find the new standard deviation and explain.

items.objective: Read frequency displays and describe center, spread, skew, and extremes.
items.prompt: Histogram bins [0,5), [5,10), [10,15) have counts 4, 8, 8. Find total count and fraction below 10.

items.objective: Read frequency displays and describe center, spread, skew, and extremes.
items.prompt: Most values cluster near 10 but a few reach 100. Describe the likely skew and a useful measure of center.

items.objective: Interpret direction and linear strength without inferring causation.
items.prompt: Which is stronger linearly: r=0.85 or r=-0.3? Explain.

items.objective: Interpret direction and linear strength without inferring causation.
items.prompt: A scatterplot has a strong curved pattern but r is near zero. Explain the apparent mismatch.

items.objective: Distinguish both, either, and at least one; use changing counts and complements.
items.prompt: A bag has 3 red and 4 blue balls. Draw two without replacement. Find P(two red).

items.objective: Distinguish both, either, and at least one; use changing counts and complements.
items.prompt: For that bag, find P(at least one red), naming the complement.
